title: 3f. Guide, proofs page, and learning steps as HTML with diagrams and examples
description: Sam prefers HTML for design documents and detailed documentation, with examples and diagrams. Convert learn/README.md (the path), guide.md, proofs.md, roles.md, possession.md, and the hello step into HTML pages in the project's document template (the one every design narrative uses, with its diagram runtime), under learn/, with a learn/index.html. Add a diagram wherever one carries the point: the two legs of a tool call through the Gateway, the shape of a use case folder, the build from Unity Catalog to the tag maps, the three parties on a call, the corpus beside the guardrails. Keep every command line and every quoted policy real and checked: the smoke test (3a) extracts commands from HTML code blocks as well as Markdown, and the quoted-policy check runs over the HTML. The landing page (3b) links the path, the guide, the proofs page, and history/.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green including the link checker and the smoke test over the HTML pages. No Markdown remains under learn/ except a one-line pointer. Every diagram is the template's declarative kind, no images.

title: 3c. README: a summary, then what you can do
description: README.md stays Markdown, since GitHub renders it, and becomes short and action-oriented: one paragraph saying what the project is, then what a reader can do, each with the command: run hello, check a use case, ask what a caller may do (check-access), put a tool call through both legs (dry-run), open a case in Cedar's playground (share), start a use case of their own (copy hello, per the guide), read how it was built (history/). Every deeper subject links to an HTML page (3f). No history, no iteration list, no file-by-file map in the README; the map lives on the landing page. Sam's writing rules apply.
acceptance_criteria: ./check.sh green including the command smoke test. The README fits on one screen before the first heading and every command in it runs.
